correctness.rationale: Every primitive idempotent of M_n(F_q) is rank-one projection, equivalent bijectively to an antiflag (P,H) with P outside H. For every nonzero e,f, eRf !=0; hence source indecomposability adjacency reduces to ef=fe=0, equivalent to Q subset H and P subset M. Count q^(n-1) nonincident hyperplanes per [n]_q point. A neighbor picks Q in H in [n-1]_q ways then M through P avoiding Q in q^(n-2) ways. For adjacent vertices the line PQ misses H intersect M, yielding [n-2]_q choices of S and q^(n-3) choices of N through PQ but missing S, so lambda=q^(n-3)[n-2]_q, valid at n=3. Edges and triangles follow by double counting; at n=3 lambda=1 implies local matchings and triangles correspond to unique side lines of noncollinear triples. Independent q=2,n=3 construction confirms 28 vertices, degree6, 84 edges, 28 triangles, lambda1. General q prime powers follow from projective incidence counts, not the finite computation.

value.rationale: The primitive-idempotent graph is a natural structural graph attached to a matrix ring. Exact uniform adjacent common-neighbor multiplicity is an edge-regularity theorem, not a tautological vertex count; it gives the entire edge and triangle census and the rigid local matching / triangle-bijection behavior in dimension three. These properties are useful for finite geometry and ring graph analysis beyond previous connectivity information.

scientific_limitations: Only induced primitive-idempotent graph, n>=3 over finite fields; no higher-rank idempotent assertion.
Prime-power generality is symbolic projective geometry, not covered by prime-field-only scripts.
